{{Nihongo|'''Seiji Shinkai'''|新海 征治|Shinkai Seiji|born July 5, 1944}} is a Japanese [[chemist]] and professor of [[Kyushu University]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://ias.kyushu-u.ac.jp/organization/index.php |title=九州大学・高等研究院・組織・メンバー(written in Japanese) |access-date=2012-05-11 |archive-date=2014-11-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129024039/http://ias.kyushu-u.ac.jp/organization/index.php |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chem-station.com/chemist-db/archives/2007/10/post-1.php|title=新海征治 Seiji Shinkai|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> and emeritus professor.

== Early life ==
Shinkai was born in [[Fukuoka prefecture]], Japan, in 1944. He completed his B.S. in 1967 and Ph.D. in 1972 from [[Kyushu University]].

== Career and research ==
He is known for his pioneering research in [[molecular self-assembly]]. Molecular self-assembly is the assembly of molecules without guidance or management from an outside source.

His main field of expertise and research interests are [[Host–guest chemistry|Host Guest Chemistry]], [[Molecular recognition|Molecular Recognition]], [[Liquid crystal|Liquid Crystals]]/Organic Gelators, Sugar Sensing/Sugar-Based [[Combinatorial chemistry|Combinatorial Chemistry]], [[Boronic acid|Boronic-acids]], Polysaccharide-Polynucleotide Interactions, Sol-Gel Transcription and Inorganic Combinatorial Chemistry.  His most recent research is related to chiral discrimination using [[Aggregation-induced emission|AIE]].

In 1979 he published the first light driven [[molecular machine]] in Tetrahedron Letters.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=1979|title=Photocontrolled extraction ability of azobenzene-bridged azacrown ether|journal=Tetrahedron Letters|volume=20|issue=47|pages=4569–4572|doi=10.1016/S0040-4039(01)86651-X|last1=Shinkai|first1=Seiji|last2=Ogawa|first2=Toshiyuki|last3=Nakaji|first3=Takahiro|last4=Kusano|first4=Yumiko|last5=Nanabe|first5=Osamu}}</ref>

To date (July 2019) he has published over 1024 original paper and 219 reviews and books.
